overview: The Committee of the Whole met to refer a free cash appropriation for parking kiosks and soil remediation, and to conduct preliminary fiscal year 2026 budget reviews for multiple city departments.

items.title: Free Cash Appropriation for Parking Kiosks and Soil Remediation
items.summary: The committee discussed a $150,859.89 free cash appropriation for Flowbird parking kiosk replacements and continued soil remediation at 448 High Street, referring the matter to the regular City Council meeting.

items.title: Recreation Department and Hormel Stadium Budget Review
items.summary: Recreation Director Kevin Bailey reviewed departmental achievements, therapeutic recreation expansion, and ice rink utility expenses; the committee approved a motion to investigate installing solar panels at the Hormel Stadium parking lot.

items.title: Assessing Department Budget Review
items.summary: Chief Assessor Jared Yagjian presented on the upcoming citywide property revaluation, historical new growth data, and the additional staffing capacity that would be required to administer a residential tax exemption.

items.title: Building Department Budget Review
items.summary: Building Commissioner Scott Vandewalle discussed rising public records requests, upcoming multi-family developments, the integration of permitting software, and initial plans for leaf blower ordinance enforcement.

items.title: City Clerk and Legislative Budgets Review
items.summary: Clerk staff discussed transition plans for online business licenses, the need for individual software subscriptions, and legislative line-item codes for agenda management systems.

items.title: Electrical Department Budget Review
items.summary: Superintendent of Wires Steve Randazzo explained a budget increase driven by rising utility meter rates and streetlight maintenance costs.

items.title: Fire Department Budget Review
items.summary: Chief Todd Evans highlighted fleet procurement backlogs, training programs, and critical staffing shortages, leading the committee to pass a motion urging the administration to seek Tufts PILOT funding for a new dive rescue team.

items.title: Insurance, Pensions, and Debt Service Budget Review
items.summary: Finance Director Bob Dickinson reviewed the city's outstanding debt obligations, an estimated 10% rate increase for employee GIC health insurance, and the city's timeline to fully fund its pension system by 2033.
